title: Orionid meteor shower to light up October skies with fiery cosmic display
excerpt: Skywatchers, get ready — one of the year's most beautiful meteor showers is back and set to light up the October night sky.
content:
THE TAKEAWAY

  • The Orionid meteor shower is expected to peak overnight from Oct. 21 to 22.
  • The meteors are known for their brightness and speed, traveling at about 41 miles per second.
  • The Orionids will be viewable from both the northern and southern hemispheres after midnight.

Skywatchers, get ready — one of the year's most beautiful meteor showers is back and set to light up the October night sky this week.

OCTOBER SKYWATCHING GUIDE: HUNTER'S MOON, METEOR SHOWERS, SATURN AT OPPOSITION AND MORE YOU CAN'T MISS

The Orionid meteor shower is expected to peak overnight from Oct. 21 to 22, delivering a spectacular display of shooting stars, according to NASA.

The Orionid meteor shower is observed in the night sky on October 22, 2025. 

(Xue Bing/VCG  / Getty Images)

The meteors are known for their brightness and speed, traveling at about 41 miles per second as they enter Earth's atmosphere.

HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER

According to NASA, these fast-moving meteors can leave behind glowing "trains," incandescent bits of debris in the wake of the meteor. These glowing bits can last anywhere from several seconds to minutes.

Some Orionids can even become fireballs, producing exceptionally bright flashes of light in the night sky.

The Orionid meteor shower is expected to peak overnight from Oct. 21 to 22. 

( Xue Bing/VCG / Getty Images)

The Orionid meteor shower occurs every year when Earth passes through a trail of shredding debris left behind by 1p/Halley’s Comet.  

During this time, the comet bits collide with the atmosphere and disintegrate, which creates fiery and colorful streaks in the sky.

'FIREBALL SEASON' EXPLAINED: WHY METEORS LIGHT UP SKIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY

Each time 1p/Halley's Comet returns to the inner solar system, its nucleus sheds ice and rocky dust into space. By October, the dust grains become the Orionids.

Orionids can  become fireballs, producing exceptionally bright flashes of light in the night sky.

(Xue Bing/VCG  / Getty Images)

1p/Halley's Comet takes about 76 years to orbit the sun. It was last visible from Earth in 1986 and is expected to return in 2061.

The Orionids will be viewable from both the northern and southern hemispheres after midnight.

For the best viewing experience, experts recommend heading to a dark location away from city lights and streetlamps.

The Orionid meteor shower occurs every year when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by Halley's Comet. 

(VCG / Getty Images)

Lie flat on your back with your feet pointing southeast if you're in the Northern Hemisphere, or northeast if you're in the Southern Hemisphere, and look up to take in as much of the sky as possible.

Allow your eyes 20 to 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness, and soon you will be treated to a spectacular celestial show.
